page: The Amazon Web Services gr6.8xlarge is an accelerated computing instance hosted on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by a dedicated 16-core, 32-thread AMD EPYC 7R13 processor operating at 3.4 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Designed around a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:8, the instance provides 256 GB of DDR4 memory clocked at 3 GHz, allocating 8 GB of RAM per vCPU. For hardware acceleration, it bundles a single NVIDIA L4 GPU from the Ada Lovelace architecture featuring 22 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local high-speed storage is integrated as a 900 GB NVMe SSD, complemented by a 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth configuration.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong capabilities in memory subsystems and specialized processing tasks. The instance achieved a strong PassMark memory score of 2,795.44 alongside single-core stress-ng performance of 2,992.38. Its cryptographic acceleration capabilities stand out with a PassMark CPU encryption score of 37,915.95, supported by hardware-level AES and VAES instruction sets. Large-block memory bandwidth benchmarks register 76.82 GB/sec for uncached reads and 43.7 GB/sec for uncached writes, while standard multi-core CPU metrics fall squarely within expected midrange performance brackets across Geekbench and stress-ng tests.

In machine learning evaluations, the integrated NVIDIA L4 GPU places the gr6.8xlarge in top-tier brackets for small to medium language model inference. For 7B parameter models, prompt evaluation reached 2,250.32 tokens per second and text generation sustained 53.58 tokens per second. Inference throughput on lightweight 135M models reached 12,218.27 prompt tokens per second and 472.22 output tokens per second. However, for 70B parameter models, memory constraints limit execution to prompt processing at 36.07 tokens per second, with large-scale generation bounded by the single GPU's 22 GB capacity.

The combination of a high-capacity 256 GB memory footprint, local NVMe caching, and dedicated Ada Lovelace acceleration makes the gr6.8xlarge technically balanced for memory-intensive AI pipelines. It is suited for real-time model serving up to medium parameter sizes, graphics and video rendering, image processing pipelines, and data-intensive analytical applications requiring local disk caching.
description: The Amazon Web Services gr6.8xlarge is an accelerated computing instance engineered for memory-dense graphics and machine learning workloads. Powered by the AWS Nitro System, it features a 16-core, 32-thread AMD EPYC 7R13 processor running at 3.4 GHz, 256 GB of DDR4 system memory with an expansive 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio, and a dedicated 900 GB NVMe SSD. Hardware acceleration is provided by an integrated NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L4 GPU equipped with 22 GB of VRAM. Supported by 25 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, benchmark results demonstrate top-tier execution in small to medium model inference, achieving 2,250.32 tokens per second on 7B prompt evaluations. The hardware configuration delivers strong cryptographic throughput and high memory bandwidth, balanced by moderate multi-core compute capability. It fits workloads requiring substantial host memory alongside GPU acceleration, including real-time AI inference, image processing, graphics virtualization, and data-intensive pipelines.
